prompt: starting a new side project: react frontend, go backend (chi router + pgx for postgres), and probably a small python data scraper later on. i want everything in one repo. i know pnpm workspaces for the js side but i'm not sure how the go part fits in — do i need to give the go app a package.json? can i share types between react and go? can you set up the repo structure?
assertions: apps/api is a native Go module: go.mod exists inside apps/api and Go code isn't forced into JS conventions
No JS dependencies injected into the Go app: apps/api has either no package.json or a thin wrapper package.json with zero runtime dependencies
Cross-language type sharing answered via schemas/codegen (OpenAPI, protobuf, or generated types), not by pretending Go can import TS types
One canonical task orchestration story spans both languages: a Makefile or thin package.json wrappers — a single coherent command set, not two competing layers
Layout keeps apps/ (deployables) and packages/ (shared JS libs) separation, with a sensible planned home for the future python scraper (e.g. apps/scraper)
Per-app env files for web and api, and docker-compose.yml (or equivalent) at the root provides Postgres for local dev
